historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal JPY mid-cycle growth for a domestic-steel-weighted conglomerate; the historical CAGRs are trough-to-above-mid-cycle (FY2021 was a COVID/steel-spread trough, FY2023 FCF was 20.7bn) and extrapolating any of them would be wrong
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 12.2% diverges >30% from revenue 5-yr CAGR 7.4% and from the 3-yr revenue CAGR of -0.5%: book value compounded off the FY2021 trough through retained earnings and the FY2022 equity issuance (share count 362.7m -> 394.5m), not through revenue growth. Not used for the forward path.
historical_growth.notes: FCF series is reported FCF (OCF less capex); SBC is nil throughout so the owner-FCF series equals the reported series. FCF CAGRs are meaningless (FY2021 base 21.6bn, FY2023 base 20.7bn): the 5-yr FCF average is ~46bn, the 3-yr average ~74bn.

scenario_narratives.base: A mid-cycle Kobe Steel: FY2027 recovers only part-way to guidance (EBITDA margin 9.8%, OP ~125bn after a 20bn Q1), then the group earns a 10% EBITDA margin on ~2% nominal growth -- Steel & Aluminum near breakeven-to-modest profit, Advanced Materials, Welding, Machinery, Engineering and Electric Power carrying the profit pool as they did in FY2026. Capex runs modestly above depreciation through the EAF transition. FCF conversion is structurally poor (~30% of EBITDA after 30% tax, capex > D&A and working-capital drag), so the terminal value is capped at 13x FCF, roughly 4x EBITDA.
scenario_narratives.bull: Guidance delivered and sustained: 2,690bn sales and 150bn OP in FY2027, margin matures to 11.5% on anti-dumping relief for domestic steel, aerospace/semiconductor-driven Advanced Materials and Machinery growth, Midrex DRI licensing, and the aluminium extrusion integration. Growth 3% fading to 1.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Q1 FY2027 collapse persists: Steel stays at breakeven under Chinese export pressure, Electric Power's windfalls fade, margin reverts to the 10-yr average 8.5%, revenue flat. Equity value is thin because net debt of 558bn and NCI sit ahead of shareholders.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kobe Steel is valued as a consolidated cyclical industrial on an owner-FCF DCF with mid-cycle margins, not on the latest year or on guidance. The stock screens cheap on book (0.63x P/B, BVPS ~3,180 yen) and on earnings (~8x FY2027 guided EPS), but the DCF says those multiples are what a 30% EBITDA-to-FCF conversion, a 558bn-yen net debt stack ahead of equity and 1-2% nominal growth deserve. Non-operating assets (211bn of investment securities, haircut 10%) and NCI are bridged explicitly; leases are in net debt; NCI is charged once; SBC is nil so house and street coincide. The 13x FCF terminal cap (about 4x EBITDA) binds in every scenario, so the valuation does not depend on a re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: at a textbook market-weighted JPY WACC (~5-6%) the Gordon value is far higher; the 13x FCF cap then does all the work. The sensitivity grid (WACC 6-10%) is the honest range.
Mid-cycle EBITDA margin: each 1pp on the 10% base is worth roughly 25bn of EBITDA, ~17bn of FCF and ~450-500 yen/share. The FY2016-FY2021 history (mean ~7.9%) argues the 8.5% bear is not the floor.
FY2027 guidance (OP 150bn) is back-half loaded after a 20bn Q1; the base takes ~125bn. Delivery would move base toward bull.
Capex: the decarbonisation programme (large-scale EAF, ammonia co-firing) was cut to ~150bn over three years but could be restored; every 0.5pp of sustained capex/sales is ~13bn/yr of FCF.
Investment securities (190bn after haircut, ~480 yen/share) are a large part of equity value; their market value moves with the Nikkei and the company is selling them down.
Electric Power segment: merchant coal generation faces carbon-pricing / decarbonisation policy risk in Japan beyond the explicit horizon.

data_sources.financials: 5406.T_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2016-FY2026 annual plus Q1 FY2027); 5406.T_Annual_FY2025.txt (company fiscal 2025 = year ended 31 Mar 2026) for cash flow components, segment capex/D&A and the FY2027 outlook; 5406.T_Quarterly_Q1-2026.txt (Q1 FY2027) for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, share counts and the revised FY2027 forecast

inputs.share_count_basis: 396,345,963 issued less 1,440,289 treasury = 394.9m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin), plus ~1.8m shares to be issued in the Kobelco Wire simplified share exchange (effective ~Sep 2026), consistent with the company's FY2027 EPS guide of 252.09 yen on 100.0bn yen profit. No potentially dilutive securities (tanshin note). Held FLAT: SBC is nil, the share exchange is the only non-SBC issuance and is already in the count.
inputs.debt_note: 30 Jun 2026: borrowings and bonds 707,200 (short-term 140,946, commercial paper 20,000, bonds 135,000, long-term borrowings 411,254) plus lease liabilities 26,801 (current 5,480 + non-current 21,321) = 734,001; cash and deposits 176,233. Ties to the company's own 'interest-bearing debt' definition (769.9bn at 31 Mar 2026 = 743,073 CSV TotalDebt + 26,843 leases).
inputs.fcf_note: FY2026 (year ended 31 Mar 2026): operating cash flow 201,683 less purchase of PP&E/intangibles 124,435 = 77,248. 5-yr reported FCF: 21.6 / 12.4 / 20.7 / 110.4 / 35.0 / 77.2bn (FY2021-FY2026) -- average ~46bn, i.e. the latest year is above mid-cycle.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in the J-GAAP consolidated cash flow statement FY2016-FY2026 (checked: 'Purchase of treasury shares' is the only equity line). SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position null.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income 3,144 (FY2026) is left out of the deduction: the company is net-debt (557.8bn), so the cash pile is not added to EV and there is nothing to double-count. The EBITDA-based component build excludes it anyway (EBITDA = operating profit + depreciation).
inputs.buyback_note: Purchase of treasury shares 3,164 in FY2026 (800 in FY2025; nil FY2019-FY2024). Not a structural repurchaser; dividends (37,468 in FY2026, 80 yen/share) are the distribution channel.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. JGB 10y ~1.7%, JPY ERP ~6%, beta ~1.2 for a leveraged steel/materials cyclical gives a cost of equity ~8.9%; after-tax cost of debt ~1.3% (interest expense 13.4bn on ~770bn interest-bearing debt, 30% tax). Market-weight WACC (~50% debt) would be ~5%; the house JPY industrial reference is ~9%. Settled at 8.0%: the house reference less ~1pp for the genuinely cheap, long-dated yen debt that funds half the capital structure. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- cyclicality, China export pressure and the Q1 guidance miss are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities 26,801 (30 Jun 2026) are inside total_debt; no lease principal is deducted from the flows; lease-asset renewal is covered by the capex % line. J-GAAP operating leases are already expensed in operating profit, so no further adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book (67,891 at 30 Jun 2026). NCI took 6.2bn of FY2026 profit (~6%); book deduction is the simpler and more conservative single charge.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Investment securities 210,994 at 30 Jun 2026 (listed cross-shareholdings at fair value plus equity-method affiliates at equity, J-GAAP). Their income (dividend income 5.2bn, equity-method profit 14.1bn in FY2026) sits below operating profit and is therefore OUTSIDE the EBITDA-based flows, so the asset goes into the bridge (matching-asset rule), at a 10% haircut for tax on embedded gains on disposal (the company realised 32.2bn of securities sales in FY2026). Retirement benefit liability 45.1bn vs retirement benefit asset 49.7bn at 31 Mar 2026 net to ~zero and are left out.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations -- routed via the dcf-methods table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'. A sum-of-the-parts was considered because of the seven-segment structure (Steel & Aluminum, Advanced Materials, Welding, Machinery, Engineering, Construction Machinery, Electric Power) and rejected: every segment is an operating business whose cash flows consolidate cleanly, there is no embedded lender/REIT/trust, and the segment note discloses ordinary profit and capex but not FCF, so a per-segment DCF would be seven guesses summed. The segment mix instead informs the mid-cycle margin: Electric Power (Kobe Power Plant units 3-4 online since FY2022-23), Machinery and Advanced Materials lift the structural EBITDA margin above the FY2016-FY2021 average (which was depressed by the 2017 quality-data scandal and COVID), while commodity Steel (ordinary profit 2.9bn in FY2026 vs 23.7bn) and Construction Machinery pull it toward the 10-yr mean. MID-CYCLE: 10-yr EBITDA margin 9.0 / 6.3 / 10.2 / 7.7 / 6.2 / 7.7 / 9.3 / 8.0 / 12.0 / 11.0 / 10.4% (FY2016-FY2026); 10-yr mean 8.9%, 5-yr mean 10.1%, FY2026 actual 10.4%. Base holds 10.0% (between the two means), bull matures to 11.5% (below the FY2024 peak 12.0%), bear reverts to 8.5% (the 10-yr mean). Guidance: FY2027 (Apr 2026-Mar 2027) revised at Q1 to net sales 2,690bn (+10.4%, from 2,560bn), operating profit 150bn (+15.5%, unchanged), net profit 100bn (unchanged), H1 OP 65bn / net profit 35bn (-44%). Q1 operating profit was 20.4bn (-34.8%) and net profit 12.2bn (-68%), so the 150bn needs an 85bn H2 -- base does not take it at face value (FY2027 EBITDA margin 9.8%, OP ~125bn); bull does. SCANDAL: the 2016-17 data falsification is legacy; no premium in the WACC, it lives in the weak-steel bear weight. TERMINAL: Gordon at 8%/1% is 14.4x FCF; the 13x cap binds in every scenario (cyclical, structurally slow domestic steel market). Current price was fetched from Yahoo at the timestamp in price_as_of; TSE regular close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: The Q1 FY2027 miss (OP -35%, net -68%) is the trend, not a blip: the 150bn guide is missed, Steel stays near breakeven as China's ~119mt of exports and a shrinking domestic construction/auto market keep spreads compressed, Electric Power loses its fuel-cost-lag gains, and the EBITDA margin reverts to the 10-yr mean of 8.5-9% and stays there. Revenue flat in nominal terms. Capex is trimmed but cannot fall below D&A for long. On these flows the leveraged balance sheet (558bn net debt) absorbs most of the enterprise value.

base.growth_note: FY2027 +7%: between the Q1 run-rate (+1.6%) and the revised 2,690bn guide (+10.4%, which carries metal-price pass-through and the Kansai Coke / Kobelco Wire consolidation); thereafter 2% fading to 1% nominal JPY -- domestic crude steel output is at multi-decade lows and the growth pockets (titanium, IP presses, Midrex DRI) are small relative to the 1tn-yen Steel & Aluminum base.
base.margin_note: FY2027 9.8% (OP ~125bn vs the 150bn guide, after a 20.4bn Q1); then 10.0% mid-cycle, between the 10-yr mean (8.9%) and the 5-yr mean (10.1%).
base.capex_note: D&A 5.0% (FY2026 123.9bn = 5.1%). Capex 5.6-5.8% in FY2027-FY2029 for the Kakogawa large-scale EAF / decarbonisation programme (3-yr plan cut to ~150bn from ~300bn) and cost inflation, fading to 5.2% -- still above D&A, because a steelmaker that spends below depreciation is shrinking.
base.tax_note: 30% cash rate = Japanese statutory effective rate (~30.6%). Loss carryforwards from FY2017/FY2020-21 are used up (FY2025 cash tax 68.3bn, FY2026 23.5bn on a 121bn ordinary profit as timing reversed); the engine never credits tax on a loss.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables + inventories exceed payables (net working capital ~25% of sales), so growth consumes cash: -20% of each year's revenue increase.

bull.narrative: FY2027 lands on guidance (2,690bn sales, OP 150bn = 10.8% EBITDA margin) and the margin matures to 11.5%, just under the FY2024 peak (12.0%), as anti-dumping duties on Chinese/Korean/Taiwanese flat steel restore domestic spreads, Advanced Materials (aerospace titanium, semiconductor aluminium) and Machinery (IP presses, 241bn backlog) keep growing, and the Nippon Light Metal extrusion integration fixes a sub-scale unit. Revenue grows 3% then 1.5%, capex is held nearer D&A.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the Q1 FY2027 print (OP -35%, net -68%) already sits well below the pace the maintained 150bn guide needs, commodity Steel is the largest segment and is near breakeven, and the balance sheet is leveraged (net debt ~2.2x EBITDA), so a margin reversion to the 10-yr mean is a live outcome, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it requires guidance delivery, anti-dumping relief AND sustained Advanced Materials/Machinery growth together. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
